request.recipient: Input Output Global / Intersect administrative treasury governance
request.what: Funding for IO: Hydra to deliver a feature-complete and hardened Hydra v2 through performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience workstreams.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade or production-ready Layer 2 scaling solution on Cardano.
The proposal requests ₳5,100,781 and states the funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
Hydra is claimed to provide sub-second finality, near-zero or zero internal fees, high throughput, and L1-grade settlement guarantees.
The document claims Hydra has powered Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost payments, and Midgard withdrawals.
The document claims provisional users evaluating Hydra include Bodega Market, Atlas Defi, Wingriders, Houselink, European Public Network, and others.
The proposal claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, about $0.17 payment transaction cost, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, making high-performance applications uncompetitive on L1.
The performance workstream claims it will achieve 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and reduce L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization.
The proposal claims Hydra applications can grow L1 fee revenue through head opening, fund addition/removal, closure, settlement transactions, and optionally routed internal fees.
The document claims many current Hydra use cases rely on the requested improvements and risk migrating to competing chains if the proposal slips.
The proposal states it aligns with treasury KPIs for TVL, monthly active users, monthly transactions, throughput capacity, reliability and uptime, annual protocol revenue, and Pillars 1, 2, 4, and 5.

summary: The document requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening and adoption work, asserting strong technical benefits and major ecosystem relevance, but most adoption, cost-benefit, and economic-return claims are asserted rather than evidenced within the supplied text.
